headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in Riyadh sofa factory fire
summary: Tragedy strikes as 16 Bangladeshi workers perish in a Saudi Arabia fire; most victims were from Naogaon, leaving families in deep grief.
details: A devastating fire tore through a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killing 16 Bangladeshi workers. Out of the victims, 13 were from Naogaon, two from Natore, and one from Rajshahi.
One victim, 28-year-old Mohan Pramanik, sent a heartbreaking final voice message to his family, asking why no one was picking up before stating, 'I will not be able to talk to you anymore.'
Another victim, Rubel Miah, had returned home in December for four months and had a newborn daughter who is now an orphan. Kalimuddin, 30, was due to return home in the month to get married.
Habibur Rahman, the sole survivor among 17 Bangladeshi workers at the factory, escaped because he was at a nearby barbershop during the fire.
According to a former worker, the factory was operating illegally, had no windows, and the doors were locked from the outside to avoid police detection, trapping the workers inside.
The victims' documents and passports were destroyed in the fire. Saudi police are now requesting photocopies of passports to return the bodies of the deceased to Bangladesh.
Local administration in Naogaon and the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment are coordinating with the embassy to ensure the bodies are brought back home quickly.
caption:
“I will not be able to talk to you anymore.”

A heartbreaking final message from one of 16 Bangladeshi workers killed in a Saudi fire.

A devastating fire tore through a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killing 16 Bangladeshi workers. Out of the victims, 13 were from Naogaon, two from Natore, and one from Rajshahi.

One victim, 28-year-old Mohan Pramanik, sent a heartbreaking final voice message to his family, asking why no one was picking up before stating, 'I will not be able to talk to you anymore.'

Another victim, Rubel Miah, had returned home in December for four months and had a newborn daughter who is now an orphan. Kalimuddin, 30, was due to return home in the month to get married.

Habibur Rahman, the sole survivor among 17 Bangladeshi workers at the factory, escaped because he was at a nearby barbershop during the fire.

According to a former worker, the factory was operating illegally, had no windows, and the doors were locked from the outside to avoid police detection, trapping the workers inside.

The victims' documents and passports were destroyed in the fire. Saudi police are now requesting photocopies of passports to return the bodies of the deceased to Bangladesh.

Local administration in Naogaon and the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment are coordinating with the embassy to ensure the bodies are brought back home quickly.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline: 726 patients admitted: Dengue hospitalisations hit record high in 24 hours
summary: Total infections in Bangladesh have crossed 20,000, with 61 deaths recorded so far, according to the DGHS.
details: At least 726 dengue patients were hospitalised across the country in the last 24 hours, marking the highest number of single-day hospitalisations recorded so far.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of dengue infections has now risen to 20,071.
The death toll from the virus stands at 61 people.
Currently, 1,443 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
